newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says trapped miners show no signs of life.
newsitem.headline: Peru says trapped miners show no signs of life.

text.p: Two miners trapped underground for over a week after a powerful earthquake have stopped showing signs of life, Peruvian officials said on Wednesday.
"Sound equipment brought from the United States is not detecting anything. There are no signals," said Civil Defence spokesman Pedro Rivera, adding the rescue operation would continue.
"We think we are close to reaching them. Let's hope it is not too late," Rivera said.
Previously the freelance miners were believed to have been signalling they were still alive by banging rocks inside the collapsed tunnel.
Experts had estimated the men would not survive beyond Wednesday. They are stuck underground at the hillside gold mine at Guanillo near Nazca, 290 miles (460 km) south of Lima.
The miners were trapped by a quake that shook southern Peru on last Tuesday, killing 14 people, injuring hundreds and leaving tens of thousands homeless.
The quake killed one miner at Moyohauca, 375 miles (600 km) south of Lima, and many more had to be dragged out of several remote mines around Nazca.
